topic_name: Abilities, predispositions, giftedness, talent and genius

241.question: Individual characteristics connected with the success of performing an activity are called...

options.B: Predispositions

242.question: The natural anatomical and physiological basis for the development of abilities is made up of...

options.B: Predispositions

options.A: They guarantee a high result without training
options.B: They unambiguously prescribe a particular profession
options.C: They can become the basis of different abilities
options.D: They serve as prerequisites for the development of abilities
options.E: They are identical to ready-made professional skills

244.question: The same keen hearing can develop in different professional directions. This expresses...

options.B: The independence of abilities from activity
options.C: The exclusively quantitative nature of giftedness
options.E: The identity of a predisposition and a talent

245.question: How are abilities and activity related?

options.A: Abilities arise independently of the demands of activity
options.B: Activity merely reveals unchangeable innate abilities
options.C: Abilities are formed and manifested in activity
options.E: Repetition of an activity guarantees any level of development

246.question: Possibilities that are not yet realized but can manifest themselves when social conditions change are called... abilities.

options.B: General

247.question: By degree of realization, an ability that is needed now and used in the activity being performed is...

options.B: Special

248.question: Justified conclusions about the development of abilities:

options.A: A change of activity can open new possibilities
options.B: The absence of manifestation proves the absence of potential
options.D: A pronounced predisposition does not guarantee the development of an ability
options.E: Development ends with the formation of the analyzers

249.question: By breadth of applicability, powers of observation, useful to a writer, a physician and a researcher, belong to... abilities.

options.B: General

250.question: Special abilities are determined primarily by...

options.A: Only the overall speed of reactions
options.B: The requirements of a particular kind of activity
options.C: The presence of any strong emotion
options.D: The predominance of one bodily component
options.E: Only the number of words learned

251.question: Giftedness is understood as a distinctive combination of abilities that provides...

options.A: The possibility of successfully performing an activity
options.B: A complete replacement of knowledge and skills
options.D: A guarantee of success regardless of preparation
options.E: The inheritance of a ready-made profession

252.question: A gifted student cannot cope with a professional task without preparation. Which conclusion is justified?

options.A: Success is determined only by general giftedness
options.B: Giftedness automatically ensures professionalism
options.C: Preparation does not affect the realization of abilities
options.D: Potential requires the mastery of knowledge and skills
options.E: Failure proves the absence of any abilities

253.question: A general factor and specific factors in the explanation of intellectual giftedness were identified by...

options.B: D. N. Uznadze

254.question: Correct correspondences between researchers and their propositions:

options.A: Spearman: a general factor and specific factors
options.B: Pavlov: the author of the concept of the intelligence quotient
options.C: Kretschmer: a two-factor model of intelligence
options.D: Ziehen: a critique of a single general ability
options.E: Stern: the ratio of mental age to chronological age

255.question: The conscious orientation of thinking toward new demands in the definition of giftedness was emphasized by...

options.B: W. Sheldon

256.question: A qualitative analysis of giftedness primarily answers the question...

options.A: What single rank a person occupies in a ranking
options.B: How to exclude the influence of the conditions of development
options.C: How a person's distinctive combination of abilities is structured
options.D: Which profession a person's heredity guarantees
options.E: How many innate professional skills a person has

257.question: A high level of special abilities that is realized in original, socially significant products is called...

options.B: An actual sensory ability

258.question: Creative achievements that open a historically new epoch in a particular field characterize...

options.B: A high level of general educability

259.question: Indicate the correct statements about giftedness and talent.

options.A: Talent presupposes a combination of abilities
options.B: Knowledge is superfluous given high giftedness
options.C: Giftedness creates a possibility, not a guarantee of success
options.D: A single isolated skill always equals talent
options.E: A social position automatically makes a person a genius

260.question: By their importance for an activity, the components of an ability that occupy the central place in performing it are called...

options.B: General

261.question: The presence of talent is most justifiably judged primarily by...

options.A: Only external features of body build
options.B: The early award of an honorary status
options.D: The results of independent, original activity

262.question: The twelve-dimensional model of properties of the nervous system, including primary and secondary properties, was proposed by...

options.B: V. D. Nebylitsyn

263.question: By level of generality, properties of an individual analyzer, rather than of the whole nervous system, are called...

options.B: General

264.question: When assessing giftedness, one should take into account:

options.B: Only the presence of a natural predisposition
options.C: The requirements of a specific activity
options.D: The complete independence of the result from instruction
options.E: The conditions of the person's development

265.question: Why is the assessment of a single ability insufficient for predicting professional success?

options.A: A single ability is not related to any activity
options.B: All abilities develop in strictly the same way
options.D: The result depends on the combination of components and on preparation
options.E: Any success is entirely predetermined by age
